#6098. How Much Does It Cost To Fly A Private Jet From New York To California?

Private jet travel has boomed in popularity since the pandemic, as more people found out how flexible and convenient it was. The time saved at airports is considerable, with all the processes streamlined, efficient, and personalized. Private jets are luxurious and very comfortable, as well as saving precious time.

As such, for high-flying business executives, celebrities, or ultra-high-net-worth individuals, flying privately offers the best experience, especially in the United States, where business jets are a firm feature. Private jet travel can be expensive, but how much does it cost to travel from New York to California?

One of the most popular destinations for private jets is Los Angeles, so let's use that as a guideline and look at some different options. Is there a cheaper way to fly private? Is it cheaper to consider private ownership or charter with an operator on a regular basis? Let's find out!

In this case, Teterboro Airport (KTEB) in New Jersey is an ideal airport for New York as it is dedicated to business jets and is just 12 miles away from Manhattan. The airport is well-supported with five FBOs available. Van Nuys Airport (KVNY) is the airport of choice for Los Angeles. It is 20 minutes from downtown. The airport sees more than 260,000 movements per year and is one of the busiest private aviation airports in the world.

According to Air Charter Advisors, chartering a private jet from New York to Los Angeles can start at around $40,000 for a one-way flight on a Cessna Citation Longitude or $50,000 for a heavy jet such as the Bombardier Challenger 604 or Dassault Falcon 2000LXS. Stratos Jets recommends the Bombardier Challenger 300 for this particular trip and estimates a cost of between $34,000 and $41,000 for a one-way flight.

Clay Lacy suggests that a round trip from New York to Los Angeles on a Gulfstream G450 may cost $102,000, and prices include the aircraft, crew, and fuel. Not included in the price are positioning flight time, landing fees, federal excise taxes, or overnight fees. A trip on a light jet between the two cities could cost $56,000, and $79,000 on a mid-size jet.

Discover private jet charter costs worldwide, top aircraft choices, and leading companies. Fly private with flexibility and luxury!

Larger and more luxurious jets with more range will command much higher hourly rates than something like a Pilatus PC-12. Of course, the longer the flight, the more fuel is used, and the crew will accrue more hours, adding more to the overall cost. The flight time between New York and LA is typically between five and a half and six and a half hours, depending on the aircraft type.

Private jets are chartered by the hour and can range from $3,500 up to $18,000 per hour. The price varies depending on the type of private jet and its size, as well as many other factors. According to Evojets, the 'ballpark' prices for chartering a private jet and their hourly rate are detailed in the table below.

Traveling at peak times or during the holidays can also influence the cost of chartering a private jet. If the aircraft needs to be repositioned to pick up the passengers or to return to base, this can result in additional costs. There may also be costs for landing fees or permits, and fuel costs can fluctuate, leading to surcharges. Other extra costs may include crew salary and per diem, accommodation and ground transport costs, and catering.

If money is no object, it is an easy process.

Looking at private ownership and operating costs, a pre-owned Gulfstream IV, for example, can be bought for around $3.2 million for an early 1990s model (production ceased in 1992), according to Liberty Jet. The budget needed per year for 200 hours would be $1,668,667. Taking into account the cost of fuel and the aircraft's speed, it equates to an average cost per mile of $19.12.

If the shortest distance in the air between New York and Los Angeles is 2,446 miles (via a distance calculator), in this case, the flight (one way) would cost $46,767.52 to operate on a Gulfstream IV that flies 200 hours a year. This does not include the initial aircraft cost, just the operating costs, fixed and variable.

Furthermore, Guardian Jet figures are based on 300 operating hours per year, annual fixed costs of $1,070,534, and variable hourly costs of $6,870.20 per hour, meaning that the flight could cost around $62,630. Of course, with private ownership, there are many variables in the equation.

As such, these figures are only estimated based on the given information and should not be considered fully accurate. There are other alternatives to both private ownership and charter: it all depends on the individual and how much they fly.

Because a single private flight can cost anything from a few thousand dollars to well over six figures, it is imperative that fliers prep ahead.

​​​One option is fractional ownership, where you can buy shares in an aircraft. There are usually 16 shares in an aircraft, and they are based on 800 flying hours a year. Therefore, you can buy 1/16th of an aircraft and acquire 50 flying hours, or 2/16ths for 100 hours, and so on. The cost will vary depending on the aircrafttype. On top of that, there are usually monthly management fees and an occupied hourly fee. All fees are fixed in advance.

A jet card or membership plan is another option. It works like a pre-paid card, where your flying hours are bought in advance and then used when needed. These are fixed hourly rates that are agreed upon in advance with a broker or operator. Of course, with these and fractional ownership, you have an aircraft at your disposal, without all the costs and hassles of ownership and paying for crew, insurance, hangar, and everything else.

Empty legs can offer another cheaper alternative to charter. These are when an aircraft is repositioned to return to base without passengers or flying empty to meet passengers somewhere else. Some charter companies will sell these at a highly discounted rate, as much as 50%, 75%, or even 90%, in order to recoup some of the costs. A search on Fly Victor showed that empty legs between New York and Los Angeles could be found for the costs detailed in the table above.

One of the cheapest ways to take advantage of the private aviation industry.

To get an accurate quote for a trip between New York and Los Angeles, a client should contact a few different charter operators or brokers to compare. It is important to have specific dates in mind, the number of passengers traveling, and any special requirements.

This can include catering, special amenities, or celebrating a special occasion. The more details, the better. A charter operator or broker will use this information to calculate the cost, which can vary based on factors like aircraft availability, fuel costs, airport fees, and the duration of your trip.

Each quote will be tailored to the client's exacting needs, based on the aircraft that are available and the current market conditions. If the client travels frequently by private jet, then private ownership is a possibility, but fractional ownership, jet cards, and memberships are also useful to avoid the extra costs and hassles of ownership. Empty legs are a more affordable alternative for a simple one-way charter at a discounted price.

When flying regularly between New York and Los Angeles, there are lots of options and varying prices, so it is important to check and compare for the most competitive price. It is always a good idea to get a few quotes from different brokers and not settle on the first price, unless the client is traveling in an emergency at the last minute.

#6097. Considering The Bilt Palladium Card? Here’s Why You Should Apply Soon…

The Bilt Palladium Card (learn more) is the most premium card in the Bilt credit card portfolio, and personally, it’s one of my all-around favorite cards (Rates & Fees). If you’ve been on the fence about picking up this very lucrative card, I’d highly recommend applying ASAP, and definitely before the end of 2026. Let me explain…

The Bilt Palladium Card is one of my favorite credit cards, and it’s the card that gets the most of my spending. Just to cover some of the very basics, the card has a $495 annual fee (Rates & Fees), and offers the following value proposition at the moment:

For me, the logic of picking up this card is pretty straightforward, and I’ve shared that in much more detail. The idea is that the combination of the 2x points plus 4% back in the form of Bilt Cash is an unrivaled return on spending, especially given the value of Bilt points. Spending on Bilt cards also earns you Bilt elite status, and that unlocks better Rent Day promotions.

On the most basic level, that Bilt Cash earns me 1x points per dollar spent on my housing payments (without any sort of fee), plus I take advantage of the Points Accelerator feature, which earns me an extra 1x points per dollar spent up to five times per year, by redeeming $200 in Bilt Cash. In other words, this card earns me 3x points on up to $25,000 of spending per year, plus I’m being rewarded on my housing spending.

Points with Bilt rack up really quickly, so if you spend quite a bit on credit cards, I do think this is tough to beat. And this doesn’t even account for the value of the hotel credit, as you can stack the credit card’s hotel credit with some Bilt Cash to get an even bigger discount on a hotel stay.

As I’ve covered, changes are coming to Bilt as of 2027. While the changes are being made in the name of “simplifying” things, I’d argue that it only creates even more complexity, at least for existing members. Essentially, starting in 2027, Bilt members will earn points for their housing payment as a percentage of their card spending, in lieu of earning 4% back in Bilt Cash on all their spending.

The good news is that through December 31, 2026, you can still opt into the old system for being rewarded, and that will then be honored in 2027 and beyond. This applies both to existing cardmembers, and those who pick up the card before then, and select this as their earnings preference.

The idea is that if you opt into this grandfathered system and have the Bilt Palladium Card:

Just as an example, I have more Bilt Cash than I can redeem (at least as someone who is scared of helicopters, and who finds Blacklane to be overpriced even with the Bilt Cash redemption options). However, the Bilt Cash I earn gets me 1x points on all my housing payments, maxed out Points Accelerator redemptions, elevated Rent Day offers, and Lyft and Walgreens redemptions, so I get $120 in credit with each business per year.

I think the Bilt Palladium can still absolutely be worth it under the new system, where you’d be rewarded on housing payments per the below, and would also earn $600 in Bilt Cash annually (starting in 2027), but without the 4% back in the form of Bilt Cash on spending.

So if the Bilt Palladium Card has at all been on your radar, this would definitely be the time to apply. After all, this is what will allow you to maximize value on the card in the long run.

Bilt is making some program changes as of 2027, which are a mixed bag. From my perspective, the biggest loss is that cardmembers are by default being switched from a system where they earn points plus flexible Bilt Cash for their spending, to one where they earn points plus rewards at a certain rate toward housing payments.

At least for me, the old system is definitely better, and the good news is that through the end of 2026, you can continue to opt into the old system of earning points plus Bilt Cash for spending, and then that will be honored in 2027 and beyond. This applies not just to those who already have the card, but also those who open the card before the end of the year. So if the Bilt Palladium Card has been on your radar, I’d recommend applying in the near future.

#6096. Influencer Uses AI To Score American First Class Upgrade… And Overpays

There’s no denying that AI holds a lot of potential to transform how we go about our every day life, both for better or worse.

People are increasingly using AI for travel planning, but here’s an interesting twist on that. Can AI help you find award flights and secure upgrades? It’s something I’d like to study in a bit more detail and write about in the coming weeks, but I just saw a post on Instagram that piqued my interest, so I figured it would make for a fun story. Consider this just a little teaser, for the time being.

An Instagram user with 1.5 million followers who promises to help people master AI has just published a video about how “ChatGPT upgraded me to first class.” Now, that’s not as exciting as it sounds on the surface. The idea is simply that ChatGPT helped someone secure an upgrade through the standard means — it’s not like ChatGPT used his/her/their charm to sweet talk someone into an upgrade by dressing up nicely. 😉

Let me actually just quote the description of the video, which covers most of the content:

What happens when you ask ChatGPT to upgrade your flight to first class?

I tried this on my flight in two weeks and it actually worked.

Go to ChatGPT and switch from Chat to Work at the top. Start a new chat and give it your airline and confirmation code.

Prompt 1:“Ask me every question you need about my credit cards, my miles, and my memberships, and map out every upgrade currency I own for this exact flight.”

ChatGPT shows you that you’ve been sitting on upgrade power this whole time without even knowing it.

Prompt 2:“Now look up my exact flight, check how empty the first class cabin is, and tell me every way I can get up there, ranked from free to cheapest.”

Prompt 3:“Now go get me the upgrade. Use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.”

ChatGPT opens its own browser, logs into your airline, and actually chases that seat for you while you sit back and do nothing.

You can watch the video for yourself below.

A post shared by Maverick Maltin | AI & ChatGPT (@mavgpt)

I don’t want to suggest AI isn’t useful, but I’d say that the example given is actually very poor. First of all, let’s be clear about what’s actually going on here. He had booked a business class ticket on American from Los Angeles (LAX) to London (LHR), and then upgraded to first class.

Now, in the first place, something isn’t fully accurate here:

Okay, maybe he edited the dates, or something, which is fine, and it’s besides the point, but as a detail oriented airline nerd, I couldn’t help but notice those things. Anyway, let’s assume this is all accurate:

To me, this is kind of where AI falls flat, and it isn’t the correct way to use it. The prompt was reportedly to “use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.” This is where I get confused — you’d think that AI would be able to scour reviews online, and see that American first class isn’t (well, or wasn’t) really viewed as a product that’s worth the premium.

If AI were really providing useful advice here, it would’ve recommend waitlisting with the systemwide upgrade, and otherwise recommending the guy save his 70,000 miles, and use them for something else. While there are definitely some strong use cases for AI, I think this is actually a pretty poor showing of what it can do.

By the way, keep in mind that under United’s updated contract of carriage, using AI to help service reservations is banned, and could potentially get your ticket canceled. Whether there’s any enforcement of that remains to be seen.

While the thought of using AI to score an upgrade might sound great, don’t count on it actually getting you the best deal. An AI whiz claims he has the secret to using AI to upgrade to first class. All AI did was use the instant upgrade offer that was available directly on American’s website, and it didn’t even encourage him to skip the upgrade due to it not being worthwhile, or waitlisting the upgrade with a systemwide upgrade, which is objectively a much better deal than 70,000 miles.

What do you make of this AI “assistance” for a first class upgrade?

In recent years, first-class, business-class and premium economy have stolen many of the headlines when it comes to air travel — and there’s a big reason for that.

Airlines have leaned heavily into premium seating, with the fancy suites and recliners serving as the biggest money-makers on the plane.

That has led to a ton of luxe new suites and features, like United's Polaris Studios which debuted earlier this year with 27-inch screens.

At the same time, we’re also seeing some intriguing new innovations in economy, too.

To be clear, the seats aren’t suddenly getting wider, and the legroom isn’t magically improving.

But a growing number of airlines are rolling out some new options and upgrades that should ultimately lead to more enjoyable flights, without the need to pay thousands of dollars (or hundreds of thousands of points).

For starters, there’s the Wi-Fi. It has long been a pain point for travelers, as they'd be stuck paying a fee for an often-spotty service.

Nearly all of the large U.S. carriers now offer — or have plans to offer — on-board internet free to members of their loyalty programs.

Most U.S. airlines are installing or preparing to install ultrafast service from Starlink, which is widely regarded as the fastest Wi-Fi in the sky today.

The days of being disconnected when you fly are fast disappearing.

Whenever I sleep on a red-eye flight in coach, I tend to wake up with a sore neck.

This year, Emirates debuted a new feature that should help.

Its "U-Dream" setup has side wings that cradle your neck as you sleep. You can see what it looks like below.

Swipe to see me trying out a "generic" version of the concept at an aviation conference last year.

If you're going to be in economy, that headrest looks like it would definitely make the experience more comfortable — especially on a long flight from the U.S. to Dubai.

Walk-up snack bars are popping up on some commercial planes, which double as a way to stretch your legs during a long flight — and get some sustenance at 35,000 feet.

United used the last row of its new Airbus A321XLR for a snack bar, which will be a nice option for passengers flying that single-aisle plane on long-haul routes.

A handful of additional U.S. carriers have announced plans to offer their snack bars in the sky in the near future. JetBlue has offered a snack "pantry" for years on its long-range planes.

Don’t want to splurge on a pricey business-class or premium economy seat?

United recently announced it would join Air New Zealand in offering a couch, of sorts, in economy.

Next year, the carrier plans to debut a product it’s calling its “Relax Row” on some long-haul flights.

Available as a paid add-on, the concept allows you to turn three economy seats into one "bed." The airline has framed this as a strong option for families traveling together.

The setup is similar to the “Skycouch" Air New Zealand has offered on its long transpacific flights for years.

United plans to outfit some of its largest twin-aisle jets with the “Relax Row,” including some Boeing 777 and 787 aircraft.

How much would you pay for a few hours of shut-eye?

Air New Zealand plans to one-up itself soon with a new bunk-bed in coach.

The new “Skynest” concept will feature two sets of bunk beds stacked three high, with a ladder to reach the upper bunks.

Passengers will be able to book a four-hour nap for an additional fee of $495.

It’s not business-class, but if your only goal is to get some sleep on a long flight from the U.S. to New Zealand, it could be well worth it.

Speaking of ultra-long journeys, Qantas is preparing to launch the world’s longest flights.

Its “Project Sunrise” service from Sydney to London is scheduled to start in October 2027. The service will be followed by flights from Sydney to New York City.

On board the ultra-long-range Airbus A350-1000, passengers won’t just find new premium seating options.

There will also be a “well-being zone,” where passengers can walk around, stretch — and maybe even do a few exercises.

That movement is crucial on flights that will span nearly a full day in the air.

Meanwhile, even as passengers board with multiple screens and devices in their bags, airlines are doubling down on seatback screens.

In the U.S., they’re already a staple on United, Delta Air Lines and JetBlue.

But carriers are also upgrading their seatback entertainment with better headphone technology, streaming services and entertainment options.

United has been working to equip all of its seatback devices with Bluetooth pairing technology, which allows passengers to connect their Apple AirPods and similar devices to the screens.

The carrier also recently rolled out a new partnership with Spotify, which lets flyers stream from their accounts on the seatback screen.

Delta, meanwhile, has launched a seatback partnership with YouTube — and is preparing to deploy new, next-generation screens with a host of new inflight features.

As all of that unfolds, American is pivoting back to screens after removing them from its planes years ago. It will be some time before they are widely available, though.

Airlines have also struck up content partnerships with major newspapers (like the Delta-Wall Street Journal tie-up) and streaming platforms (like United’s with Apple TV+).

We’ve come a long way from the days when the whole plane would watch the same movie on communal screens.

#6092. How Endeavor Air First Officers Reach Delta Air Lines After 24 Months As Captain With No Extra Interview

For aspiring airline pilots, securing a position at a regional carrier is often the first major step toward flying for a major airline. However, Endeavor Air offers something that makes its career pathway particularly attractive: an established route to Delta Air Lines that allows eligible pilots to advance without completing another interview or additional testing. The opportunity is especially significant for pilots who want to build their experience while working toward a long-term position at a major US carrier. Under its Career Advancement Program, Endeavor Air pilots can become eligible for this pathway after completing 24 months as a captain. This arrangement gives first officers a clearly defined career objective, although reaching that milestone requires completing training, upgrading to captain, and meeting the applicable program requirements. With regional pilot salaries also increasing, Endeavor Air has become an interesting option for pilots weighing immediate compensation against future career opportunities.

The financial appeal of regional airlines has changed considerably since 2020, when starting salaries for first officers at some carriers were substantially lower than today's figures. Historically, new regional pilots could expect hourly rates around $30, making the first few years of an airline career financially challenging. However, staffing shortages, increased competition for qualified pilots, and changes in industry-wide compensation have transformed the market.

In 2026, regional first officer hourly rates are considerably higher, with some carriers offering approximately $100 or more per flight hour. Endeavor Air is particularly competitive, with its reported first-year first officer rate reaching $105.08 per flight hour. This represents a substantial improvement over older compensation figures and places the airline among the more financially attractive regional operators for newly hired pilots.

Using a monthly guarantee of approximately 75 flight hours, a first officer earning $105.08 per hour could generate around $94,572 in annual base pay. This calculation does not include signing bonuses, additional flying, per diem payments, or other potential compensation. Actual earnings depend on the applicable pay agreement, scheduling, and individual circumstances, but the guaranteed-hour calculation provides a useful starting point when comparing regional airline opportunities.

Other regional operators have also increased their compensation to remain competitive. Air Wisconsin, for example, has reported a starting first officer rate of approximately $96 per hour, translating into estimated first-year earnings between $92,000 and $110,000, depending on additional compensation. Signing bonuses also vary considerably, with some reported offers ranging from $5,000 to $15,000, while larger packages incorporating retention incentives can reach approximately $45,000.

While compensation is an important consideration, Endeavor Air's relationship with Delta Air Lines is arguably its most distinctive career advantage. The two airlines have an established Career Advancement Program, commonly referred to as CAP, which provides qualifying Endeavor Air pilots with a structured pathway toward employment at Delta Air Lines. Rather than relying entirely on the uncertainty of applying through the traditional recruitment process, eligible pilots have access to a defined advancement opportunity.

The most important milestone in this arrangement is completing 24 months as a captain at Endeavor Air. This means the eligibility clock is connected to captain service, rather than simply the date a pilot initially joins the airline as a first officer. Consequently, pilots must account for their initial training, time spent building experience, and the period required to upgrade before they can reach the qualifying milestone.

For eligible pilots, the program offers a significant advantage because the transition does not require another conventional Delta Air Lines interview or additional testing under the CAP pathway. This removes an important element of uncertainty that normally accompanies a competitive mainline airline application. However, the arrangement should not be interpreted as an unconditional job offer from the first day of regional employment, since pilots must still satisfy the program's applicable eligibility and qualification requirements.

This distinction makes Endeavor Air particularly appealing to pilots who already view Delta Air Lines as their preferred long-term employer. The opportunity provides a clearer career direction, while allowing pilots to gain valuable airline experience and earn a competitive salary along the way. It also demonstrates how a regional airline relationship can influence a pilot's decision beyond the immediate considerations of pay, aircraft, and base location. Endeavor Air operates regional flights on behalf of Delta Connection, the SkyTeam carrier's regional subsidiary.

For a newly hired first officer, the journey toward Delta Air Lines begins with successfully completing the airline's initial training and operating experience requirements. New pilots must become familiar with company procedures, aircraft systems, operational standards, and the responsibilities associated with flying scheduled regional services. This initial period is essential because it establishes the professional foundation required for progression within the airline.

The next significant step is accumulating the experience and qualifications needed to upgrade to captain. Regional airlines have traditionally provided relatively accessible upgrade opportunities compared with some larger carriers, although the exact timeline depends on staffing requirements, pilot seniority, training capacity, and operational circumstances. Industry estimates commonly place regional captain upgrades within approximately 18 to 24 months, but individual progression can vary.

An upgrade involves considerably more than receiving a new job title. First officers must demonstrate the knowledge, judgment, leadership, and technical ability required to command an aircraft. Captain training includes additional responsibilities relating to flight preparation, crew coordination, operational decision-making, and regulatory compliance. Successful completion of the required training and evaluations is necessary before a pilot can operate as captain.

Once upgraded, the pilot begins accumulating the 24 months of captain service associated with the Career Advancement Program. This is an important detail for prospective applicants because the total time between joining Endeavor Air and reaching CAP eligibility can be substantially longer than two years. A pilot should therefore consider the entire progression timeline rather than assuming that 24 months of employment automatically provides access to Delta Air Lines.

The latest data from ch-aviation shows that Endeavor Air currently operates a fleet of 145 Bombardier aircraft, made up of the following aircraft types:

Moving from a regional airline to a major carrier normally involves a competitive recruitment process. Pilots applying independently must typically submit an application, meet the hiring requirements, complete assessments, and participate in an interview. Even experienced regional captain may face uncertainty because hiring decisions depend on airline staffing requirements and the competitiveness of the applicant pool.

Endeavor Air's Career Advancement Program changes this dynamic by establishing a more direct route for qualifying pilots. The absence of an additional interview or testing requirement through the program can make a considerable difference to someone planning a long-term aviation career. Instead of repeatedly preparing applications and interviews, eligible pilots can concentrate on meeting the established requirements and performing their existing responsibilities.

This does not mean that every Endeavor Air pilot automatically transfers to Delta Air Lines after completing the required period. Program eligibility, applicable contractual conditions, professional standards, and any other requirements remain important. Pilots should also review the current official program documentation to understand the precise conditions governing their individual circumstances, rather than relying exclusively on general descriptions of the pathway.

Nevertheless, the arrangement provides a level of career visibility that can be difficult to find elsewhere in the regional airline industry. For pilots who want to fly for Delta Air Lines, the ability to work toward a defined advancement opportunity can be more attractive than relying solely on the open recruitment market. It also makes the regional experience feel like a structured stage of a longer career rather than an isolated employment opportunity.

The improved compensation available at regional airlines has made the time spent building experience more financially manageable. At Endeavor Air, a reported first-year first officer rate of $105.08 per hour produces approximately $95,000 in annual base compensation when calculated using a 75-hour monthly guarantee. This is a substantial improvement compared with the lower salaries associated with regional aviation in previous decades.

However, pilots should examine the entire compensation package rather than focusing exclusively on hourly pay. Signing bonuses, retention incentives, health insurance, retirement contributions, vacation provisions, and other benefits can influence the overall value of an employment offer. Different carriers also structure their compensation differently, meaning that two apparently similar hourly rates do not necessarily produce identical financial outcomes.

Retirement benefits are another important consideration when comparing regional employment with a future mainline position. Major airlines such as Delta Air Lines have established retirement programs that can make long-term employment particularly attractive. An often-discussed feature of major airline compensation is the 18% direct retirement contribution available under certain arrangements, although the applicable terms and eligibility conditions should always be checked against current plan documentation.

For Endeavor Air pilots, these financial considerations must be balanced against the potential value of reaching Delta Air Lines. A competitive regional salary provides income during the experience-building stage, while the CAP pathway offers a structured opportunity to pursue a mainline career. This combination can make the initial regional years more appealing than they might appear when considering hourly compensation alone.

Although the Career Advancement Program is an important attraction, prospective pilots should understand that joining Endeavor Air does not immediately guarantee a transfer to Delta Air Lines. The process involves several stages, beginning with meeting the airline's hiring requirements and successfully completing initial training. Pilots must then progress through their first officer responsibilities and qualify for an upgrade to captain before beginning the required 24-month period.

The timeline can also be affected by circumstances beyond an individual pilot's control. Training availability, aircraft requirements, staffing levels, and seniority can influence when an upgrade becomes possible. Consequently, two pilots hired around the same time may not necessarily reach captain status simultaneously. Anyone evaluating the opportunity should avoid treating an estimated upgrade timeline as a contractual guarantee.

It is equally important to understand that the CAP pathway is different from an ordinary application to Delta Air Lines. Its value comes from the specific advancement arrangement between the airlines, including the absence of an additional interview and testing process for eligible participants. Pilots should carefully review Endeavor Air's official Career Advancement Program information and confirm the current requirements with the airline before making employment decisions.

Found an error? Send it info@simpleflying.com so it can be corrected.

Ultimately, Endeavor Air provides an appealing combination of competitive regional compensation, valuable airline experience, and a defined opportunity to advance to Delta Air Lines. For a first officer seeking a long-term career with a major US airline, the possibility of becoming eligible after 24 months as an Endeavor Air captain represents a significant advantage. The pathway still requires dedication, successful progression, and patience, but it offers a clearer destination than the traditional approach of independently competing for every mainline vacancy.

#6091. Sanders: ‘Medicare for All’ will be HELP priority

Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., holds a news conference in the Capitol on Nov. 10. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call)

Saying that “Medicare for All” is no longer “a radical idea,” Sen. Bernie Sanders said Wednesday that he would prioritize passing the universal health care plan if he assumes the chairmanship of the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee next year as expected.

Democrats could bring it about through the filibuster-proof budget reconciliation process, the Vermont independent and avowed democratic socialist told reporters. And the idea could be buoyed by an influx of progressive lawmakers elected in the midterms.

Sanders said Medicare for All is gaining support from voters across the country who are looking to overhaul the American health care system as costs have soared. Democrats on the committee will move the legislation “as aggressively as we can, as rapidly as we can,” he said.

His version, introduced in April and referred to the Senate Finance Committee, would implement the universal health care system over four years. In the first year, the the age of Medicare eligibility would drop to 55 from 65, while coverage would expand to include dental, hearing and vision care. The bill would also provide coverage for eligible children during the first year.

The age of eligibility would fall another 10 years in each of the following years until the fourth year, when coverage would be extended to all Americans.

“If there has ever been a time in the modern history of our country . . . to address the crises facing working families, this is that time,” Sanders said, noting that Democrats will have a 56-44 majority when the 120th Congress begins in January, the largest margin for either party in 16 years.

Sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., along with nine other Senate Democrats, last week offered an alternative Medicare expansion plan, which would lower the eligibility to those ages 50 and up.

While who will be leading Senate Democrats is still an open question — Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is challenging Charles E. Schumer of New York, who has been the top Senate Democrat since 2017 — Sanders said he is confident the Medicare for All bill will get to the Senate floor, “no matter who the [Senate majority] leader is.” Sanders previously expressed opposition to Schumer leading the conference.

Asked about efforts to extend the Affordable Care Act enhanced subsidies, Sanders responded he’s “all in.” However, he added “the American people and elected officials understand the current health care system is broken.”

Subsidies that help enrollees pay for health care premiums on the ACA exchanges were expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic, but these enhanced credits expired at the end of last year, raising costs for many who relied on them to help defray costs.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, nominated on Wednesday to be speaker next year, previously outlined broader health care priorities such as extending the ACA tax credits and reversing Medicaid cuts enacted in Republicans' reconciliation package last year. When asked Tuesday how far Democrats want to lower the Medicare eligibility age, Jeffries responded, “that’s all part of an ongoing conversation.”

In addition to expanding Medicare coverage, Sanders reiterated his push to lower prescription drug prices. The Vermont lawmaker previously introduced legislation aimed at reducing the cost of brand name prescription drugs by linking domestic prices to international price benchmarks.

To enact some of the agenda, Sanders may have to court Republicans.

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., said last week that he plans to serve as the top Republican on the HELP committee next year. Sanders said Wednesday that his likely GOP counterpart “has shown an enormous amount of courage in taking on Republican leadership year after year.”

Sanders added that although Paul may have a different viewpoint from himself on committee issues, he looks forward to finding common ground.

#6090. Alaska Airlines Flight Delayed Hours After ICE Jet Bridge Brawl In Seattle

An Alaska Airlines flight was delayed by hours after masked ICE agents stormed the jet bridge of a departing flight to arrest a Mexican national who allegedly had a work permit had overstayed his visa (you know, “the worst of the worst”). This ended up turning into a huge jet bridge melee, leading to additional arrests, as ICE claims that someone hurled hot coffee at the officers.

In the end, the flight was delayed by hours, as the crew was no longer fit to fly, and the Port of Seattle is outraged. This is quite the story, as flagged by PYOK.

This incident happened on the morning of Saturday, November 21, 2026, and involves Alaska Airlines flight AS1306, scheduled to operate from Seattle (SEA) to Los Angeles (LAX).

This was first reported by a passenger on the flight, who explained that “ICE agents just arrested multiple people at SeaTac Airport inside the jet bridge as we were all boarding,” and went on to explain that they were “deplaning because the crew is being replaced due to poor morale.”

ICE agents just arrested multiple people at SeaTac Airport inside the jet bridge as we were all boarding. Now deplaning because the crew is being replaced due to poor morale @CNN @nytimes @seattletimes

Video taken from the jet bridge shows masked ICE agents trying to arrest people on the jet bridge.

Masked ICE agents detained two people on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as passengers were boarding a flight. Alaska Airlines said ICE officers gave them no advance notice of the operation. pic.twitter.com/r44WPTvGdv

As a result of this incident, the Alaska flight ended up being delayed by hours. It was initially supposed to depart at 8:10AM and arrive at 11:01AM, but instead, departed at 11:03AM and arrived at 1:36PM.

On November 21, 2026, at approximately 8:05 a.m. PST, ICE officers conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws.

During the arrest other travelers began to obstruct and assault our law enforcement officers—a federal crime and a felony. One passenger hurled hot coffee on the officers. Other passengers began obstructing federal officers.

The individual who threw the hot coffee was identified as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, an illegal alien from Mexico and visa overstay. She was subsequently arrested as well. She will be charged with assaulting a federal officer.

Assaulting and obstructing law enforcement is a crime and a felony. Secretary Mullin has been clear: anyone who assaults or obstructs law enforcement will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the fullest extent of the law. Our brave law enforcement is facing more than a 1,600% increase in assaults, 3,300% increase in vehicular attacks, and an 8,000% increase in death threats against them. This violence must end.

On November 21, 2026, at approximately 8:05 a.m. PST, ICE officers conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws. During the arrest other travelers began to… https://t.co/nXiBxAqIJ5

The Port of Seattle expressed its outrage about the incident, releasing the following statement:

We are outraged about this morning’s incident involving ICE and two passengers as travelers boarded AS 1306 to Los Angeles. Immigration enforcement actions at SEA are conducted without the Port’s participation or knowledge. The Port has continually asked, and local federal immigration authorities have previously agreed to protocols at SEA, and we are in conversation with DHS on whether any of these protocols were breached. However, the Port remains committed to the safety of all of our travelers and staff and airline team. This incident was not only distressing for the affected family but the passengers around them, and Port officials continue to engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred.

Washington Governor Bob Ferguson was also angry, as he held a press conference about what happened, and released the following statement:

ICE is completely and totally out of control. Like many Americans, I’m outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight, creating chaos in our communities. Today’s actions at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport are just the latest example of ICE’s deeply un-American tactics. I’ll have more to say this afternoon.

Meanwhile Alaska Airlines took a more toned down approach, and just expressed “concern,” releasing the following statement:

There’s simply no arguing that in terms of public sentiment, the tides have turned in terms of immigration enforcement, with even Trump recently admitting “I think it might be too tough.”

Q: You think your deportation policy went too far?Trump: I think it might be too tough. pic.twitter.com/NKhFjZKxnd

No matter how you feel about deportations as such, having them go down in this way for someone who simply overstayed their visa is a step too far, in my opinion. I mean, it’s one thing if we’re talking about a violent criminal on some sort of watch list, but that’s clearly not the case here.

Our four-year-old is currently at the age where he asks “why” in response to everything… and he has a lot of good questions that often make me step back and think “oh, that’s a good point.” I put myself in the situation of being on the jet bridge here as a parent, and trying to explain what was going on.

And here’s the thing — it’s one thing if these people were in uniform and identifying themselves, but when you have people who refuse to identify themselves, it’s an especially bad look. It reminds me of another incident we recently saw at Las Vegas Airport (LAS). Like, is this person being robbed in the terminal, or is this an official law enforcement operation?

A post shared by Chris Motley (@motleymodel)

On Saturday, an Alaska Airlines flight was delayed by a few hours after ICE agents stormed a jet bridge to arrest someone, leading to a larger fight, which also caused more arrests. It’s one thing if such a disruptive operation were targeting a violent criminal, but is this really the way that someone who overstays a visa should be apprehended?

The Port of Seattle has expressed outrage over how this was handled, while ICE is outraged at how its “brave law enforcement” is facing increasing violence from the public.

The Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard® is American’s primary co-branded business credit card. We’re currently seeing an excellent limited time welcome offer, which is in line with the highest ever offer that we’ve seen on the card.

When the bonus offers more than 75,000 miles — whether through additional miles or a travel credit — it meets our criteria for applying.

The Capital One Venture Business card is a straightforward option for business owners who want consistent travel rewards without having to track bonus categories. With a $95 annual fee, it offers simple earning rates, easy-to-use credits and flexible redemption options that help offset the cost year after year.

While it doesn’t come with premium perks like lounge access, its simplicity and solid earning structure make it a reliable long-term choice for everyday business spending.

The Venture Business's launch offer of up to 150,000 miles (75,000 miles after spending $7,500 on purchases in the first three months, plus an additional 75,000 miles after spending $30,000 on purchases in the first six months) is the best offer we've seen so far.

As a recently launched card, the Venture Business has only two bonus offers. Since there’s limited historical data, we recommend applying when the bonus is over 100,000 miles.

With plentiful, easy-to-understand perks, the Capital One Venture X is a no-brainer for all travelers, from luxury seekers to the more budget-minded, and the card practically pays for itself year after year.

Though the card carries a $395 annual fee, it offers a $300 annual credit toward bookings made through Capital One Travel and rewards cardholders with 10,000 bonus miles each account anniversary.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Venture X:

The highest offer we've seen on this card offered 100,000 bonus miles earned after spending $10,000 on purchases within the first six months of account opening.

When the bonus offer is 75,000 miles or higher, it's a good time to apply.

Learn more: Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card

The Venture X Business carries the same $395 annual fee as the personal version and offers the same major perks, including a $300 annual travel credit for bookings made through Capital One Business Travel and access to Capital One and participating Priority Pass lounges. It also carries the same earning rates as the Venture X.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Venture X Business:

The highest offer we've seen on this card is up to 400,000 bonus miles: Earn 200,000 miles after spending $30,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening, plus an additional 200,000 miles after spending $150,000 on purchases in the first six months.

When the bonus offer is for more than 150,000 miles, it meets our criteria for applying.

Learn more: Capital One Venture X Business

While it comes with fewer perks, the Capital One VentureOne Rewards offers the same great redemption options as its sister cards, the Capital One Venture Rewards and the Capital One Venture X, with no annual fee. You’ll earn a flat 1.25 miles per dollar spent on everyday purchases.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One VentureOne Rewards:

The highest offer we've seen allowed new cardholders to earn 40,000 bonus miles after spending $1,000 in the first three months of account opening.

When the bonus offers more than 20,000 miles — whether through additional miles or a travel credit — it meets our criteria for applying.

Learn more: Capital One VentureOne Rewards Credit Card

The biggest downsides to cash-back cards are low earning rates and a lack of bonus categories, but that’s definitely not true of the Capital One Savor Cash Rewards.

For no annual fee, the Savor offers strong cash-back earning rates on popular and often overlooked categories, including 3% back on dining, entertainment and popular streaming services.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Savor Cash Rewards:

The highest offer we've seen included a $100 Capital One Travel credit to use in the first year. Plus, new cardholders could receive a $200 cash bonus after spending $500 on purchases within the first three months of account opening.

When the bonus offer is $250 or more, it meets our criteria for applying.

Learn more: Capital One Savor Cash Rewards Credit Card

The Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards is another great card with no annual fee. It earns a reliable 1.5% cash back on all purchases, making it a perfect go-to card for the odd purchase that doesn’t fit in any bonus categories.

While many other cards offer higher earning potential in specific spending categories, this card offers the safety of knowing you’ll earn a solid 1.5% back no matter what you buy.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards:

The highest offer we've seen included a $100 Capital One Travel credit to use in the first year. Plus, new cardholders could receive a $200 cash bonus after spending $500 on purchases within the first three months of account opening.

When the bonus offer is $200 or higher, it meets our criteria for applying.

Learn more: Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card

The Capital One Spark Cash Plus earns 2% cash back on all purchases and is ideal for business owners who want to earn reliable cash-back rewards on all their expenses. It is worth noting that this is a no-preset-spending-limit card, meaning cardholders must pay off their balances in full each month.

The card has a modest $150 annual fee that can be refunded after spending at least $150,000 in your card anniversary year.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Spark Cash Plus:

The highest welcome offer we've seen on this card offered up to $3,000: $500 after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening and $2,500 after spending $50,000 on purchases in the first six months from account opening.

When the bonus is $2,000 or higher, it meets our application criteria.

The Capital One Spark Cash earns 5% cash back on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel and 2% cash back on all other purchases. With the flat rate earning structure, the card is ideal for businesses with spending across different categories.

The card has a $0 introductory annual fee for the first year, then a $95 annual fee.

The Spark Cash is a traditional credit card that allows cardholders to carry a balance, offering more flexibility for businesses that don’t want to pay their balance in full each month.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Spark Cash:

The highest welcome offer we've seen on this card is $1,500 in cash back after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening.

When the bonus exceeds $1,000, it meets our application threshold.

The Capital One Spark Cash Select is a solid option for small-business owners who want to earn straightforward cash-back rewards without paying an annual fee.

The card earns unlimited 1.5% cash back on all purchases, plus 5% cash back on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel.

Here are the offers we've seen on the Capital One Spark Cash Select:

The highest welcome offer we've seen on this card is $750 cash back after spending $6,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening.

When the bonus exceeds $500, it meets our application threshold.

Learn more: Capital One Spark Cash Select

Possibly, but Capital One restricts who is eligible to earn a welcome bonus, and the exact terms vary by card.

For several Capital One cards, you won't be eligible if you've received a new cardmember bonus on the same card — or, in some cases, another card in the same family — within the past 48 months. For example, the Venture Rewards terms exclude applicants who have received a new cardmember bonus on the Venture Rewards or Venture X within the past 48 months.

Because these restrictions vary among cards and can change, check the specific card's current offer terms before applying.

Capital One welcome offers can fluctuate, so it can sometimes make sense to hold off on applying. While there’s no guarantee that a better offer will come along, looking at a card’s offer history can help you decide whether to apply now or wait.

At the moment, we’re seeing a new member bonus for those who register for an account, making it the ideal time to sign-up, if you haven’t done so already. In particular, this pairs very nicely with the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard® (learn more) limited time welcome bonus, which offers 75,000 AAdvantage miles upon completing minimum spending.

Through December 31, 2026, the AAdvantage Business program is offering 10,000 AAdvantage bonus miles to anyone who registers for the program with promotion code BNS10K. Bonus miles will post within six to eight weeks following the successful enrollment in the program.

For what it’s worth, we did see a bonus of 15,000 miles several weeks ago, but that’s no longer available, and this bonus is much better than usual, as there isn’t ordinarily a standard bonus for becoming a member.

I should mention that in order to be eligible to participate in the AAdvantage Business program, you need to have a business in the United States or Canada with a Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN) or Business Number. However, even small businesses are eligible for this program, so that’s pretty awesome.

There’s no activity required to earn the 10,000 bonus miles in your AAdvantage Business account. Let me emphasize that with AAdvantage Business, miles are accrued to the business, and can then be shared with any company member, so they can redeem through their personal AAdvantage account.

There’s one main catch with the AAdvantage Business program, which is that in order to actually redeem the rewards you earn, you need to meet one of two activity requirements:

There’s the opportunity to really maximize value here by taking advantage of two promotions. So there’s value to taking advantage of both of these promotions:

There are many reasons to apply for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card, and the unique double dipping opportunity cardmembers are eligible for, which has made this one of my go-to cards for everyday spending.

The AAdvantage Business program is offering 10,000 bonus miles to new businesses that sign-up with promotion code BNS10K. Assuming you’re eligible, this is absolutely worth taking advantage of.

The only catch is that in order to actually cash out those miles from your business account, you need to have qualifying activity. That could include having five travelers spend $5,000 in a year, or there’s the easier option, which is just to pick up the Citi AAdvantage Business Card. Just make sure you open the business account before you apply for the credit card, so that your card will then automatically correctly link to the account.

#6085. Restored to Calder’s plan, the clouds are spinning again

Sen. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., speaks during a ceremony marking the restoration of Alexander Calder’s Mountains and Clouds sculpture in the Hart Senate Office Building atrium on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call)

The day after Alexander Calder presented his plan for a public art display in the Hart Building’s nine-story atrium to the Architect of the Capitol, he died.

Fifty years later, Alexander S.C. Rower felt a sense of awe as he stared up at his grandfather’s work, finally restored to what he had envisioned.

“It’s totally phenomenal,” he said, pointing up at the now-moving clouds as he spoke, spinning his finger around. “It’s not entertainment, but it’s trying to emulate naturalness, trying to emulate what nature would do.”

It was a long time coming for Rower, who remembers traveling to the Capitol in his 20s for the original dedication of the Mountains and Clouds sculpture in 1987. The mobile portion stopped rotating as Calder intended in the 1990s, and it was ultimately removed in 2014 after being deemed unsafe by the Architect of the Capitol. Millions of dollars in private philanthropy later, Calder’s clouds are spinning again.

Rower was back on the Hill on Wednesday for an event celebrating the restoration, joining Architect of the Capitol Thomas Austin, Sens. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., Angus King, I-Maine, and James Lankford, R-Okla., and the project’s donors. As the speakers addressed the crowd, the clouds began to speed up slightly. Onlookers gathered on the balconies overlooking the atrium and peeked through office windows. Attendees left with tote bags emblazoned with images of Calder’s art.

According to Rower, who leads the Calder Foundation dedicated to preserving and interpreting his grandfather’s art, the mobile is rotating on a 15-hour cycle that is “totally variable.”

“It can go a little faster; it can go a little slower,” he said. “I told the team today that during lunchtime, I want it to speed up just a little bit because everyone’s going to lunch. There’ll be … a lot of activity passing through, and then right at 2:30, well, let’s make it go quieter.”

It was a labor of love for those involved, and not an inexpensive one. Jon and Kim Shirley funded the $12 million restoration. Because the pieces were so large, they were transported on an extra-wide load truck and driven at a speed of 35 miles per hour from Michigan.

“We had to call every senator or governor that we knew on that route, which went through seven states, to get permissions,” he said. “That was a huge thing to overcome, and it all happened over a weekend. So my wife was actually on the phone with a governor’s wife on Saturday evening. The next day, he called up his Department of Transportation and got a permit.”

Christian Quilici, who helped manage the project on behalf of the Shirleys and said he serves as a liaison between the foundation and Congress, said the hardest part of the project was the size of it.

“We had to tear the wall down on C Street, which nobody really thought of in the beginning,” he said. “Nobody got how big this was until it showed up on their doorstep.”

Quilici said he spent years educating at least 30 different senators about the quest to reunite the mobile with the stationary mountains left behind. Some of the biggest champions were seated in the front row at Wednesday’s event, including Senate Democratic Whip Richard J. Durbin. Absent was Sen. Christopher S. Murphy, D-Conn., who has been away from the Capitol while recovering from a stroke but has been a supporter of the sculpture’s restoration for years, pressing former acting Architect of the Capitol Joseph DiPietro on it at a 2024 Senate Legislative Branch Appropriations budget hearing.

“Is there any chance that before I leave the Senate, or at least before I die, we can get the clouds back up there?” Murphy said at the time.

Padilla read a letter on Wednesday from Murphy, whose state was Calder’s home for much of his life.

“This statue is actually a statement on our democracy, that we have big pieces of monumental art right in the middle of our most important and most iconic government buildings. To get this piece of art restored to how it was designed by the artist, well, that’s good for Connecticut. But I also like to think … it’s good for democracy too,” Murphy’s statement said.

The restoration was funded entirely by donations from the Shirleys, who are prominent Calder collectors, according to Rower.

“It’s very emotional to see the work completed after 10 years of us working so hard with the Architect of the Capitol and Calder Foundation. It’s a very overpowering, overwhelming emotion,” said Kim Shirley.

In addition to helping fund the project, she’s a former Senate staffer who worked in Hart before Calder’s work was installed. Years after her time in the Senate was over, her husband Jon wanted to show her the sculpture, now filling the space she used to walk through every day.

But when the two arrived, the clouds weren’t hanging from the ceiling like they were supposed to be. He called up Rower, who was a friend of his, and said he wanted to get them back to how Calder intended. On Wednesday, the three of them stood together in Hart, looking up.

Technological and engineering advancements allowed for newer, lighter clouds to be built and be safe to hang from the ceiling.

“Before it was like a bulb, it looked like a hoagie sandwich, and now it looks just really sharp, like a razor cutting through space, which was Calder’s intention,” Rower said.

According to Rower, it involved laser-measuring the original model of Mountains and Clouds sitting in a glass case nearby in the Hart atrium. The new clouds, he said, are made of carbon fiber.

“These are giant things up in the air, and they’re just so gentle and subtle,” he said.

Younger Hill staffers don’t know a time with clouds. But for those who have spent decades in the building, it was a special moment to see them spin, as Lankford told the crowd.

“I can’t tell you how many tour groups that I’ve walked through this building and I pointed to this, and I said it’s only half there, and would take them over to the little model that’s right over here, and say this is what it’s supposed to look like,” said the senator, a former Hill staffer himself.

Standing under his grandfather’s sculpture, Rower found himself quoting the man responsible for it all.

“I find that everything I do, if it is made for a particular spot, is more successful,” he said, gazing up at it.

#6084. Rakuten New Member Bonus: $50 Referral Offer & How To Maximize It

Rakuten is my favorite online shopping portal, and if you’re not using it, you’re leaving rewards on the table. Through December 31, 2026, if you join Rakuten through a qualifying referral link and spend $50 within the first 90 days, you’ll receive a $50 bonus. The person referring you can also receive $50. This is even an opportunity to earn Amex Membership Rewards points or Bilt Points at a very favorable ratio.

Taking advantage of this Rakuten sign-up bonus is truly a no-brainer, as I’d view this as a way to get $50 worth of stuff for (basically) free. For that matter, you’re missing out more broadly if you’re not earning additional rewards for your online shopping, beyond what you earn with your credit card.

In this post I’d like to go over all the details of Rakuten, including how the Rakuten referral bonus works, and the easiest way to maximize it (as it’s really easy to take advantage of, even if you don’t think you have an immediate purchase in mind).

Link: Sign-up for a Rakuten account with a best-ever $50 bonus

Rakuten is a free online shopping and rewards platform that pays users either cash back or points for the shopping they do online. Rakuten partners with over 3,500 online retailers, many of which are well known, ranging from Lowe’s, to Nike, to Target. The Rakuten shopping portal concept is simple — if you click through from Rakuten to the partner website, Rakuten tracks the purchase and gets paid a commission, and then you get a reward as well.

Note that as a consumer, Rakuten is free to use. The commission is paid by the business, so you’ll pay the same price you’d pay if you just went directly to the retailer’s website. To maximize your savings, you can even download the Rakuten browser extension, which will automatically notify you when you can earn extra rewards.

I should mention that there are several online shopping portals out there to choose from, so Rakuten isn’t the only one. Personally I find that Rakuten is my favorite because it has among the largest selection of partners, it gives you the flexibility to earn cash back or points, and I also find the earnings rates to be very competitive.

It can always pay to use a site like Cashback Monitor to compare the earnings rates for retailers across portals, so that you’re maximizing your rewards. In some situations you may be better off using other portals, so it’s always worth understanding what your options are.

Through December 31, 2026, Rakuten is offering a generous elevated refer-a-friend bonus. Specifically, if you refer a friend to Rakuten and they spend $50 within the first 90 days, then both the person referring and the person being referred each receive $50.

This is truly a best-ever bonus, as we’ve previously only seen a bonus of up to $40 — though admittedly this offer has stuck around for quite some time.

This is a very good deal. Essentially Rakuten is giving out $100 total for a $50 purchase, between the person referring and the person being referred. Long term you can potentially get even more value with Rakuten, as rewards can be converted into Amex or Bilt Points.

Actually earning the $50 Rakuten sign-up bonus is really straightforward:

What’s the timeline with which you’ll actually receive the rewards? With Rakuten you’re paid (either in cash or points) once quarterly, and there’s a cutoff for payments, per the below chart.

Rakuten partners with literally thousands of retailers, and an eligible purchase worth at least $50 with any eligible retail partner would qualify. When you click over to the partner site, just make sure you keep an eye on any exclusions, since some types of purchases may not qualify for rewards.

There are also often amazing opportunities to earn up to 100% back or 100x points with select retailers, which is a rate at which I’d gladly buy points all day long, without even factoring in the service being sold. So I take advantage of these deals all the time, even if I don’t actually value the product.

If you’re not interested in that and don’t have anything you need to buy right now, there’s another creative option. There are easy ways to unlock the $50 bonus, including simply purchasing a $50 gift card through giftcards.com. This is so easy — you can pick up a $50 gift card with a variety of retailers, and then you’ll receive $50 in cash.

To briefly explain that process, you’d enter giftcards.com in the search bar at the top of Rakuten’s website.

Then click the “Shop Now” button, which will take you to giftcards.com. All your purchases while on that site will automatically be tracked.

The website sells a variety of gift cards with popular retailers, including DoorDash, Uber, Delta, Southwest, Hulu, Netflix, Dominos, and many more.

For example, you could buy a $50 DoorDash gift card at face value, and the code will be delivered by email within minutes.

Once the purchase is complete, you should see Rakuten automatically tracking the purchase.

Within an hour the purchase should be fully reflected — the Rakuten account will show a credit in the amount of the sign-up bonus, plus the rewards for the actual purchase (which will vary based on whether you choose to earn cash or points). As a standard, giftcards.com offers either 1% cash back, or one point per dollar spent, but sometimes we see increased offers (like right now).

Taking advantage of this is the obvious choice, in my opinion:

The reason that Rakuten is my favorite shopping portal is because Rakuten rewards can be converted into Amex Membership Rewards points or Bilt Rewards points. The exact way this works depends on the currency you choose to earn.

With the Rakuten and Amex Membership Rewards partnership, you can consistently earn one point in lieu of one cent, assuming you have an Amex card that earns Membership Rewards points. So if a retailer offers 10% cash back, you can instead earn 10x Amex points.

Based on my latest points valuations, Amex Membership Rewards points are worth 1.7 cents each, because of all the ways there are to redeem the points for first and business class international travel, while getting outsized value. To me that increases the value of the rewards by 70%.

This just requires changing one setting in your account, so it’s super easy. The only thing to be aware of is that this points earning opportunity doesn’t apply to the welcome bonus, but does apply to all spending beyond that.

That’s not the only opportunity, though. The Rakuten and Bilt Rewards partnership lets members earn Bilt Rewards points in lieu of cash back. Bilt elite members can earn one point in lieu of every one cent, while non-elite members can earn one point in lieu of every two cents. Much like Amex Membership Rewards points, I also value Bilt Rewards points at 1.7 cents each, as there are also many good uses of this points currency.

What’s cool here is that your cash back can retroactively be converted into Bilt Points for the entire Rakuten “payout” period (roughly quarterly), and that means even the refer-a-friend bonus can be converted into points.

If you have the choice between one Amex point or one Bilt point, I think many people might prefer the latter, given the value of the rewards, plus how hard they are to earn. However, if the ratio isn’t one point per cent, then I’d go with the Amex partnership instead.

Beyond the rewards you earn directly with Rakuten, your spending with retailers can of course also earn credit card rewards.

Rakuten’s co-branded Amex card is among the best cards for Rakuten spending, as it earns 4% cash back on those purchases, on up to $10,000 per calendar year. Beyond that, purchases with online retailers typically don’t qualify for any exciting bonus categories, so most consumers will want to use one of the best cards for everyday spending.

All information about the Rakuten Amex card has been collected independently by OMAAT.

For personal cards, this would include options like the Bilt Palladium Card (learn more) (Rates & Fees), Chase Freedom Unlimited® (learn more), Citi Double Cash® Card (learn more), Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card (learn more), and Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card (learn more). For business cards, The Blue Business® Plus Credit Card from American Express (learn more) and Capital One Venture X Business (learn more) are among the best.

Of course there are exceptions, since Rakuten also partners with some brands that may be in categories eligible for bonus rewards on some cards. There are a couple more Rakuten tips I should mention:

Once you join Rakuten, you too can then refer friends and family members, and earn an unlimited number of referral bonuses. Finding your link is easy. Just log into your Rakuten account, and then click on the “Refer & Earn” button at the top left. Then you can either email them an invitation, or you can just send them the URL, and they can apply through that.

OMAAT readers are welcome to leave their referral links in the comments section below.

Rakuten is my favorite online shopping portal, and the company is currently offering its best-ever new member bonus. Through December 31, 2026, the Rakuten sign-up bonus is for $50 — this is a great bonus, and it’s exclusively available if you’re referred by another member with an eligible link.

Since only a $50 purchase is required for the Rakuten referral bonus, that’s like getting $50 worth of stuff more or less for free. Then long term you can even earn Amex Membership Rewards points or Bilt Rewards points in place of cash back, which I value significantly more. If you don’t yet have a Rakuten account, this is the time to sign up.

Believe it or not, Thanksgiving is around the corner. Families around the country are working on their grocery lists — and maybe keeping an eye on the wild shopping days that come after we dine with family and friends. If you're hoping to snag some great travel deals for Black Friday, Cyber Monday and Travel Tuesday, TPG has a dedicated page where you can find our favorite deals.

And if you need a little inspiration for your next vacation, we just released our annual Where to Go list for 2027. This year's list ranges from Texas Hill Country to Tunisia and from the Cayman Islands to Kazakhstan.

Now, here's the hotel news you need to know about from this week.

Hyatt is expanding its lifestyle footprint with the opening of the first Andaz in Australia. The Andaz Gold Coast, located in sunny Queensland, will have 202 rooms and plans to "redefine coastal luxury through a distinctive blend of expressive Australian design and immersive experiences inspired by the people, places, and creative spirit of the Gold Coast," according to a statement from Hyatt. The property is near the beaches of Broadbeach, and features a series of bars and restaurants, plus a lively pool club offering live music and community-focused barbecues.

Also in Queensland, Brisbane will welcome a Park Hyatt in 2031, ahead of the 2032 Brisbane Olympics. Brisbane is one of my favorite cities, so I can't wait (though I'll have to) for the 201-room property not far from Suncorp Stadium, which will host a series of soccer and rugby events. Many details about the property are still under wraps, but if it's even half as great as the Park Hyatt Sydney, we know it'll be a great hotel.

If you haven't had the chance to visit Houston, I can't recommend it enough. The city is home to diverse cultures, incredible food and the Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo, one of the biggest rodeos in the world. If you find yourself in Beyoncé's hometown, consider a stay at the JW Marriott Houston Downtown, which just completed a years-long head-to-toe remodel. The hotel now features fresh rooms, including 56 new rooms, a redesigned lobby restaurant and a total revamp of the hotel's food and beverage offerings.

Monti, my favorite neighborhood in Rome, feels like stepping back in time. Or, at least into a movie set, thanks to its beautiful vine-covered walls, cobblestone streets and lively energy near the Colosseum. In 2028, it'll also be home to Hortus Monti Rome, part of Hilton's upscale LXR Hotels & Resorts. The hotel is spread across six historic Umbertine-era buildings, according to a statement from Hilton and features a central garden, a spa, bars and restaurants and more.

Until then, Hilton fans should check into Rome Cavalieri, one of the most popular Waldorf Astoria hotels in the world.

The Coke versus Pepsi debate is a serious one, and people tend to have strong opinions about which is better. While I'm a Diet Dr. Pepper fanatic myself, it looks like Hyatt is doubling down on its relationship with Pepsi. The company just renewed its contract, making PepsiCo the preferred beverage partner across 700 Hyatt properties in the United States. The agreement also extends to certain PepsiCo snack products.

Earlier this year, Marriott ousted Pepsi and made Coca-Cola its "global beverage partner across several categories, including carbonated soft drinks and a growing range of hydration and functional beverages."
